entries.dialogueText: "Given the serious topic we're addressing, an early start might be just what we need."

entries.dialogueText: I gestured towards the seat.

entries.speaker: Narrator

entries.dialogueText: I was sipping my morning coffee and enjoying a quiet moment of solitude when Deivid arrived, characteristically early.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Not at all, Deivid. On the contrar..."
entries.dialogueText: "Not at all, Deivid. On the contrary, we've now got an extra few minutes to strategize before the meeting."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The recent abrogation in the Grand..."
entries.dialogueText: The recent abrogation in the Grand National Assembly, coupled with ongoing dialogues with Gasom, had only served to amplify the discourse surrounding the legislation.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""I appreciate your understanding, M..."
entries.dialogueText: "I appreciate your understanding, Mr. President. It's high time we addressed these pressing matters regarding the EPA."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I'm relieved to hear that, Anton.”"
entries.dialogueText: “I'm relieved to hear that, Anton.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Thank you, Mr. President.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you, Mr. President.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""I depart earlier for my appointmen..."
entries.dialogueText: "I depart earlier for my appointments nowadays, as the stairs of the capital have become more of a challenge than I would like to admit."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Your wisdom rings true. It's been..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your wisdom rings true. It's been quite a rollercoaster since the election, hasn't it?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Rest assured, Mr. Wisci. I intend..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rest assured, Mr. Wisci. I intend to navigate these challenges with more finesse than my predecessors."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The Maroon District and the minist..."
entries.dialogueText: “The Maroon District and the ministerial buildings are dispersed in a very artificial way. No wonder it takes longer.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“It's nothing to be ashamed of, Dei..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's nothing to be ashamed of, Deivid. Would you like some coffee or tea?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Well, Deivid, it's not the stairs..."
entries.dialogueText: "Well, Deivid, it's not the stairs we're battling, but the relentless march of time."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""I've already had my tea today, as..."
entries.dialogueText: "I've already had my tea today, as per my doctor's advice. She suggests chamomile in the morning and sage tea in the evening for optimal health."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Reflecting on the years I've spent..."
entries.dialogueText: "Reflecting on the years I've spent within these walls is a journey in itself. From the time my father first brought me here during the reign of the King, right up to the present."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""It wasn't always like this, you kn..."
entries.dialogueText: "It wasn't always like this, you know. Before Tarquin Soll and his architect Herman Equa gave this area a neo-classical facelift and a new name, it used to be known as the Republic District. "

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I will support you to the end of y..."
entries.dialogueText: “I will support you to the end of your term and beyond if my health allows.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""I trust you're faring well. Sordla..."
entries.dialogueText: "I trust you're faring well. Sordland is akin to a wild mustang — complex, spirited, and ever elusive to rein in."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Or perhaps a stubborn mountain goa..."
entries.dialogueText: "Or perhaps a stubborn mountain goat, unbudging and headstrong."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""A public servant is bound by one p..."
entries.dialogueText: "A public servant is bound by one principle alone. To serve, to be the voice and hand of the people."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Listening to the doctor does bring..."
entries.dialogueText: "Listening to the doctor does bring me some comfort. It feels as though my throat has been refreshed thanks to her."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A colossal zeppelin traversed the s..."
entries.dialogueText: A colossal zeppelin traversed the sky above the Maroon District. For a fleeting moment, it blotted out the sun before gently veering to the left, letting light flood the office once more.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I will do my best to support you t..."
entries.dialogueText: “I will do my best to support you to the end of your term. This country deserves a fresh start and not a descent into the darkness of the distant past.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""I often ponder what will endure of..."
entries.dialogueText: "I often ponder what will endure of our actions and identities. Do they hold any significance in the grand scheme of things?"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "His gaze drifted, locking onto some..."
entries.dialogueText: His gaze drifted, locking onto something beyond the window.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""I recall those days with such clar..."
entries.dialogueText: "I recall those days with such clarity. The city was a vision of beauty, its people radiant with hope. But the civil war shattered our Sordish Dream, exposing the darkest parts of our nature."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“My grandmother was a farmer. Throu..."
entries.dialogueText: “My grandmother was a farmer. Through her, I know that sturdy stubbornness and why the mystical Sordish Mountain Goat is our people's soul animal.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I need loyal people to make the ch..."
entries.dialogueText: “I need loyal people to make the change this country deserves.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The longest roads are travelled ea..."
entries.dialogueText: “The longest roads are travelled easier with the dearest fellows.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Your expertise is very welcome in..."
entries.dialogueText: “Your expertise is very welcome in this administration. People abroad keep praising you.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He punctuated his statement with a..."
entries.dialogueText: He punctuated his statement with a cough, then reached for a glass of water and took a sip.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""You crossed paths with Herman Equa..."
entries.dialogueText: "You crossed paths with Herman Equa at Holsord State University, didn't you? He was a mentor to many. I recall our discussions about the future at the Kabaret Lachaven, with him and Heron Garaci."

entries.dialogueText: “I know you were just a student at the Lachaven Business School, far from Holsord. But the armed rebels did reach your area.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I know you were just a student at..."
entries.dialogueText: “I know you were just a student at the Deyr University of Culture. Witnessing what true oppression was like.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""I did not agree with all of the me..."
entries.dialogueText: "I did not agree with all of the measures enacted by the technocratic government of that era. But some were undeniably effective."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""In the end, it took a collective e..."
entries.dialogueText: "In the end, it took a collective effort to reassemble our nation's fragmented pieces. I'm sure you remember those dark days yourself."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""A mountain goat, you say? Interest..."
entries.dialogueText: "A mountain goat, you say? Interesting analogy. They are indeed resilient, much like our nation."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Just as the conversation hit a paus..."
entries.dialogueText: Just as the conversation hit a pause, the door swung open and the other ministers arrived. Symon Holl entered first with a confident stride.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Good morning, Mr. President. Deivi..."
entries.dialogueText: "Good morning, Mr. President. Deivid. I trust the discussion is progressing well?"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Lileas followed closely behind. She..."
entries.dialogueText: Lileas followed closely behind. She walked in with an air of calm authority, her gaze sweeping across the room.

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""Gentlemen. I hope I'm not interrup..."
entries.dialogueText: "Gentlemen. I hope I'm not interrupting anything crucial."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Still, one must credit Tarquin Sol..."
entries.dialogueText: "Still, one must credit Tarquin Soll for extricating our nation from the ashes."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Perhaps history would have taken a..."
entries.dialogueText: "Perhaps history would have taken a different course if the Izzam Incident hadn't happened."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""We are deeply indebted to him. The..."
entries.dialogueText: "We are deeply indebted to him. The principles of Sollism hold a special place in my heart and continue to guide my decisions."

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I kept listening to him."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Those were formative years for me...."
entries.dialogueText: "Those were formative years for me. Equa and Garaci left an indelible mark on my outlook."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""It's interesting how those academi..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's interesting how those academic days shape our perspectives, isn't it?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""It was a surreal time, studying bu..."
entries.dialogueText: "It was a surreal time, studying business principles while chaos ensued just a few miles away."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Those disturbances did not deter m..."
entries.dialogueText: "Those disturbances did not deter me from my studies. In fact, they reinforced the importance of my education."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""It was a difficult period. But it..."
entries.dialogueText: "It was a difficult period. But it was also a reminder of the change I wished to see in Sordland."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Those experiences have shaped me,..."
entries.dialogueText: "Those experiences have shaped me, and they continue to inform my decisions as president."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""In retrospect, an earlier resignat..."
entries.dialogueText: "In retrospect, an earlier resignation might have been beneficial. His ingrained traditions seem to have done more harm than good in the long run."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Indeed, the Izzam Incident is a re..."
entries.dialogueText: "Indeed, the Izzam Incident is a reminder of how unforeseen events can rapidly change the course of a nation."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""No one can deny Soll's contributio..."
entries.dialogueText: "No one can deny Soll's contribution. His leadership was instrumental in rebuilding Sordland."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""There's merit to that argument. Th..."
entries.dialogueText: "There's merit to that argument. The lingering influence of Soll's traditions may have hampered Alphonso's ability to bring about the changes he envisioned."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Sollism indeed has its virtues, an..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sollism indeed has its virtues, and it's clear that Soll's legacy continues to resonate with many. The challenge for us is to learn from the past while forging our own path forward."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""It turned us away from the path of..."
entries.dialogueText: "It turned us away from the path of reform, but we still worked hard to create the Sordland my father had envisioned."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Ah. I still remember the first air..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ah. I still remember the first airships in Sordland. We purchased them from Qinal after the war, during the birth of what Soll called the 'Second Republic'."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Our infrastructure lay in ruins, a..."
entries.dialogueText: "Our infrastructure lay in ruins, and those zeppelins offered a much-needed lifeline, a chance to traverse and rebuild. And then, thanks to our research council's diligent efforts, we started manufacturing our own in Gelsord."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""It's fascinating to think how much..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's fascinating to think how much we depended on foreign help after the war. We've come a long way since then."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The manufacturing of zeppelins in..."
entries.dialogueText: "The manufacturing of zeppelins in Gelsord was truly a turning point."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Do you think we might have leaned..."
entries.dialogueText: "Do you think we might have leaned too heavily on zeppelins for our transportation needs? Perhaps we should have invested more in rebuilding our roads and railways."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""We were in a desperate state then...."
entries.dialogueText: "We were in a desperate state then. But remember, it is often in our darkest hours that we find the strength to rise again."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""You're quite right. It symbolized..."
entries.dialogueText: "You're quite right. It symbolized our resilience, our determination to regain our footing. It was a beacon of hope, signaling the revival of our battered industry."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""An interesting point. Perhaps a mo..."
entries.dialogueText: "An interesting point. Perhaps a more balanced approach would have served us better. In the aftermath of the civil war, it was often about immediate solutions, and the zeppelins offered just that."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""At the time, the destroyed roads,..."
entries.dialogueText: "At the time, the destroyed roads, bridges and all made air travel the most suitable option. But now I am glad that your presidency is focusing on building up our infrastructure."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""But over time, he drifted away fro..."
entries.dialogueText: "But over time, he drifted away from the ideals of reform and progress that my father held so dear."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Our reliance on others was tempora..."
entries.dialogueText: "Our reliance on others was temporary, a stepping stone towards the self-sufficiency we achieved with the National Autarky Plan. Even though it had downsides, I still consider it a success."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A pause fell over the room. Deivid'..."
entries.dialogueText: A pause fell over the room. Deivid's gaze landed on the portrait of Tarquin Soll hanging in the Presidential Office.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Those same amendments also opened..."
entries.dialogueText: "Those same amendments also opened the door to corruption."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Do you think the EPA still holds r..."
entries.dialogueText: "Do you think the EPA still holds relevance today, or should we consider a complete overhaul?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The NAP was a cornerstone for our..."
entries.dialogueText: "The NAP was a cornerstone for our post-war recovery. I wonder, could we have done more with it?"

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Hindsight, as they say. We did wha..."
entries.dialogueText: "Hindsight, as they say. We did what we believed was best at the time. Could we have done more? Perhaps."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Indeed, no policy is immune to mis..."
entries.dialogueText: "Indeed, no policy is immune to misuse. Alphonso's amendments were ambitious, but they also left room for exploitation. We must remain vigilant against such risks."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""The EPA has its roots in a differe..."
entries.dialogueText: "The EPA has its roots in a different era. While some of its principles may still hold, we must not shy away from revising it in light of our current needs and challenges."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "His eyes lingered on the stern face..."
entries.dialogueText: His eyes lingered on the stern face of the old leader. A sigh escaped his lips.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Now, when I think of the EPA, my m..."
entries.dialogueText: "Now, when I think of the EPA, my mind is carried back to the formative years of post-civil war Holsord in the 1930s. The debates, the passion, the potential for transformation—it was a time of renewed optimism."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""It is our duty now to learn from t..."
entries.dialogueText: "It is our duty now to learn from the past and strive for a better future. What applied back then won't apply to now."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""His visionary zeal succumbed to th..."
entries.dialogueText: "His visionary zeal succumbed to the more pragmatic, more conservative, and sometimes even regressive, dictates of political survival."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Life in Holsord back then was toug..."
entries.dialogueText: "Life in Holsord back then was tough. Electricity blackouts, ruined infrastructure, unemployment, gangs..."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I remember that Soll's pardons to..."
entries.dialogueText: "I remember that Soll's pardons to armed rebels did a lot to quell the rampant unrest."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I can see why the Energy Protectio..."
entries.dialogueText: "I can see why the Energy Protection Act was so crucial at the time. We had to safeguard our energy sector from foreign interference, especially in the context of the post-civil-war economic situation."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""It was a challenging period, yes,..."
entries.dialogueText: "It was a challenging period, yes, but we persevered together as a nation."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Soll's pardons were undoubtedly a..."
entries.dialogueText: "Soll's pardons were undoubtedly a contentious move, as they sparked debates about the extent of amnesty granted and the implications for justice."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Yes, the EPA helped ensure that th..."
entries.dialogueText: "Yes, the EPA helped ensure that the sector remained under our control, limiting the extent of ownership of foreign powers such as Rumburg or Lespia."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""In a way, Tarquin Soll did carry o..."
entries.dialogueText: "In a way, Tarquin Soll did carry on my father's legacy. Under his leadership, we transitioned from a military government to a civilian one, and experienced our first multi-party elections."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“I am sure at least some of my wrin..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am sure at least some of my wrinkles today were a direct result of my non-stop debates with them.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“Stability and order is important t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Stability and order is important to our nation. Yet sometimes disorder is necessary for change."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: "“The minorities of this nation have..."
entries.dialogueText: “The minorities of this nation have suffered particularly.”

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""My father was a visionary, a man w..."
entries.dialogueText: "My father was a visionary, a man who sought to modernize Sordland into a secular, democratic republic. I've always been guided by his principles."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Your father's legacy still looms l..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your father's legacy still looms large. Has it influenced your own views?"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Deivid turned towards the large, fr..."
entries.dialogueText: Deivid turned towards the large, framed portrait of his father, Artor Sanaco Wisci, hanging on the wall. Painted with rich, warm hues, it captured the first President of Sordland in his prime.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A spark of determination gleamed in..."
entries.dialogueText: A spark of determination gleamed in his eyes, and his mouth was set in a gentle, firm smile – a reflection of his belief in a better future for our country.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""His ability to mobilize public sup..."
entries.dialogueText: "His ability to mobilize public support for revolutionary change has been a constant inspiration to me."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Sordland wouldn't be what it is to..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sordland wouldn't be what it is today without your father."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Yes, my father's leadership laid t..."
entries.dialogueText: "Yes, my father's leadership laid the foundation for the Sordland we know. His policies were aimed at building a secular and democratic state where every citizen's rights are protected."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""He believed in a Sordland that was..."
entries.dialogueText: "He believed in a Sordland that was modern and forward-looking. Everything he did was aimed at fostering progress, even his controversial embrace of foreign ideologies."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Artor S. Wisci. It's a shame that..."
entries.dialogueText: "Artor S. Wisci. It's a shame that such an influential man died under such tragic circumstances."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Losing my father in the Holsord Pr..."
entries.dialogueText: "Losing my father in the Holsord Prison fire was a turning point in my life. I was shocked when he was arrested, and his sudden death left a deep void."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""But it also ignited a fire in me,..."
entries.dialogueText: "But it also ignited a fire in me, a resolve to carry on his legacy and fight for the principles he stood for. The circumstances of his death are a stark reminder of the lengths to which those in power can go to silence dissent."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""One more concern. Gus and Mikail i..."
entries.dialogueText: "One more concern. Gus and Mikail informed me that you have given President Alphonso assurances about not imposing stricter EPA regulations."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Given the economic climate, it mig..."
entries.dialogueText: "Given the economic climate, it might be prudent not to destabilize the system. Imposing a reduction of the threshold would irreversibly harm Gasom."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""There is no need to be destructive..."
entries.dialogueText: "There is no need to be destructive in an already dangerous economy that could spiral downward."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I understand the need for economic..."
entries.dialogueText: "I understand the need for economic stability. But I'm reconsidering my promise now that I know all the facts."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""Our actions should be guided by th..."
entries.dialogueText: "Our actions should be guided by the best interests of our nation."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""We must consider the far-reaching..."
entries.dialogueText: "We must consider the far-reaching implications of our actions. Especially in light of our recent dealings with Gasom."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Mr. President, your decision to po..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, your decision to position Sordland as the sole Gasom investor certainly gives us more control over the gas sector, but it has increased our financial burden significantly. We must review our fiscal policies."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Mr. President, your decision to pu..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, your decision to pursue co-investment with Rizia allows us to distribute the financial burden and mitigate risks. It also promotes regional cooperation, aligning well with our fiscal policies."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Mr. President, your decision not t..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, your decision not to invest has certainly reduced our immediate financial responsibilities, but we may have missed an opportunity."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Our administration needs to protec..."
entries.dialogueText: "Our administration needs to protect the jobs of Gasom workers and this investment ensures that. I have little interest beyond this."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Rizia might not be the best partne..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rizia might not be the best partner given our history with them, but we have to take a balanced approach with our budget and economy."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""By allowing Rizia to monopolize th..."
entries.dialogueText: "By allowing Rizia to monopolize the energy sector, we've indirectly promoted capitalist exploitation. We must remain vigilant and ensure our people are not subjugated to foreign profiteering."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""A reduction in the EPA could pave..."
entries.dialogueText: "A reduction in the EPA could pave the way for potential profits from shares, whereas total removal may invite an unpredictable rush for the remaining 45%."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""If we remove the Energy Protection..."
entries.dialogueText: "If we remove the Energy Protection Act entirely, our 30 percent investment could potentially be overshadowed by foreign investors. However, it could also maximize our returns if foreign investment floods in."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""Full removal of the EPA is a risk...."
entries.dialogueText: "Full removal of the EPA is a risk. Foreign investors could buy up larger stakes than our own. We might lose control over Gasom."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Eliminating the EPA could stimulat..."
entries.dialogueText: "Eliminating the EPA could stimulate our economy, increasing the value of our 30 percent stake. But losing control over Gasom would be a heavy blow."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Foreign influence in Gasom, if not..."
entries.dialogueText: "Foreign influence in Gasom, if not managed correctly, could lead to a dilution of Sordland's control in the energy sector."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Even though we're sharing the inve..."
entries.dialogueText: "Even though we're sharing the investment with Rizia, we should still prioritize Sordish control. Let's consider reducing the foreign ownership limit."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""I'm glad you see the risks, Mr. Pr..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm glad you see the risks, Mr. President. Keeping our energy sector in Sordish hands should be our priority."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Reducing the foreign ownership lim..."
entries.dialogueText: "Reducing the foreign ownership limit might safeguard our control, but it could limit our potential for economic growth."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Completely removing the EPA could..."
entries.dialogueText: "Completely removing the EPA could upset our foreign relations, particularly with market economies. We must consider the implications of such an aggressive move."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""We could remove the threshold enti..."
entries.dialogueText: "We could remove the threshold entirely, opening up to more foreign investment. But we'd need to be prepared for all the diplomatic consequences that may follow."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""It could also lead to a volatile s..."
entries.dialogueText: "It could also lead to a volatile situation in terms of our foreign relations."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Full removal of the threshold is a..."
entries.dialogueText: "Full removal of the threshold is an extremely bold move. It could lead to a significant increase in foreign investment, but we must also consider the risks."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""Total removal of the threshold is..."
entries.dialogueText: "Total removal of the threshold is a dangerous proposition. It would make us vulnerable to foreign influence and could lead to the loss of our energy independence."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Our priority should be balancing t..."
entries.dialogueText: "Our priority should be balancing the need for economic growth with maintaining national sovereignty. Perhaps a phased approach to increasing foreign ownership could be the answer."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Mr. President, it's time for us to..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, it's time for us to make a decision. What will we do with the EPA?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""We need to balance our commitment..."
entries.dialogueText: "We need to balance our commitment to Alphonso with the needs of our nation."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""There's also the matter of interna..."
entries.dialogueText: "There's also the matter of international perception. We should be careful not to appear as if we're making policy based on corporate interests alone."

entries.title: Player: ""I'd like to clear my mind before t..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'd like to clear my mind before the ministers arrive."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""As you wish, Mr. President. I will..."
entries.dialogueText: "As you wish, Mr. President. I will be as silent as a mouse."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Then the door swung open, ushering..."
entries.dialogueText: Then the door swung open, ushering in the arrival of the other ministers. Symon Holl entered first with a confident stride.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "It was nice to sit in silence and e..."
entries.dialogueText: It was nice to sit in silence and enjoy each other's company. Time passed.

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""I believe much of his urgency was..."
entries.dialogueText: "I believe much of his urgency was motivated by his own desire to escape Soll's shadow. For better or worse, he managed it."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Mr. President, Lileas, shall we re..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, Lileas, shall we return to the subject of the EPA?"

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""In my view, it was a necessary ste..."
entries.dialogueText: "In my view, it was a necessary step to attract foreign investment and stimulate our economy."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""Think about it, Mr. President. If..."
entries.dialogueText: "Think about it, Mr. President. If any one of those countries -- but especially Rumburg -- gains control of our energy sector, they could cut off our power at any moment."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""We would also be forced to comply..."
entries.dialogueText: "We would also be forced to comply with any decision they made regarding prices or environmental measures."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""Don't forget about the importance..."
entries.dialogueText: "Don't forget about the importance of economic security. In a globalized world, economic strength can be just as critical as military might."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: ""But yes, it's essential to maintai..."
entries.dialogueText: "But yes, it's essential to maintain strict oversight and regulations to ensure national interests aren't compromised."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""At times the window of change is o..."
entries.dialogueText: "At times the window of change is only very small. And now that you and I are in the cabinet, we can promote the change we truly advocate for."

entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""I think you are misguided in this..."
entries.dialogueText: "I think you are misguided in this way of thinking. But of course we're allowed to hold differing opinions."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I share your view. Soll's old poli..."
entries.dialogueText: "I share your view. Soll's old policy was choking the growth of Sordish energy businesses."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""Many others also saw Alphonso's ch..."
entries.dialogueText: "Many others also saw Alphonso's changes as necessary. Though they did not pass without a great deal of controversy."

entries.speaker: Deivid Wisci
entries.title: Deivid Wisci: ""In the end, the changes to the EPA..."
entries.dialogueText: "In the end, the changes to the EPA did facilitate foreign investment, even if they didn't lead to a drastic uptick in economic growth."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I don't only respect the Assembly'..."
entries.dialogueText: "I don't only respect the Assembly's decision. I wholeheartedly support it."
